ranking_account.finding: Eligible universals are encountered from target first, then lexically named original axioms, Gamma occurrences and selected literal outputs. Their retained pool shares maximum_demands with unrelated demand-frame budget. This deliberately presents the target itself as a possible UI antecedent before axiom-based alternatives.

connected tests only whether a proposed member has exactly the marked root row/formula. It never tests whether an external pending formula is the same root. novel tests literal absence from selected outputs, not proof progress or established information. overlap rewards literal target subtrees, even repeated in a licence/antecedent. A connected root-restating family can therefore dominate a detached axiom/licence even with a larger member count: connected is the first lexicographic coordinate, member penalty last.

An anchor has only one retained family. A connected self-demand family replaces its detached licence under the same full anchor because its score is lexicographically higher. emit has already reconstructed/cloned members/ports/binding before the duplicate-anchor comparison, charging work even when the result is discarded.

Generic \(P:=\forall v\,E(v)\) can yield an incident UI licence \(P\to E(v)\), MP requiring open \(P\), then UG returning \(P\). Physical row references remain strictly prior and every primitive may be lawful, but the open logical obligation restates the desired conclusion. This is a heuristic-quality defect, not an accepted circular proof: the required input is never a fact merely from its mark.

Separate ranking from generation. A useful axiom-based connected family, IF generated, may also have connected=1 and compete on later coordinates. This note does not assert that such a family was enumerated in the target run or that a better ordering would finish. Many potentially useful alternatives can be absent from the finite generated prefix altogether.

starvation_account.finding: Initial roots are in physical row order; only their prefix enters frames. The loop expands ALL earlier alignments of one frame before moving to the next. A small frame cap can thus be filled by the first root even though other initial roots are already queued. All candidate/compatible-suffix rebuilding happens eagerly before any advice stream is serviced.

The finite term pool is parameter-first, then traversal-order input subterms, then a canonical grammar prefix only if space remains. An omitted term is unavailable to all schemas in that invocation. Full subtree/universal gathering precedes term selection, so even a tiny term cap does not bound that preparation to a tiny cost. No term-carrier completeness claim is warranted.

licence_stream nests universal outside term: with \(T\) retained terms, its first later universal gets a turn only after \(T\) earlier descriptor yields. Thus \(R<T\) stream rounds cannot even reach it. ui_mp_stream additionally drains all source rows for a matching pair before the next term/universal; skipped chosen-row alignments yield None and still consume a round. Increasing a term cap can delay later universals instead of broadening the reached prefix.

The outer loop gives one next(stream) per live stream per round. It is fair only across those already-created generator objects. A next call can perform unequal guarded work before yielding; nested occurrence/term/middle/equality-row/antecedent-row transport loops are similarly biased toward their lexicographic prefixes. None yields count as descriptor steps too.

Global work/native interruption can occur during eager preparation or any expensive next/emit. Any Timeout makes the WHOLE batch UNKNOWN even if partial proposals exist; those stay diagnostic-only. On normal return, top-score truncation and anchor-only dedup can still hide diverse interfaces. No empty/truncated stream or omitted family proves nonexistence.
